turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’m so tired of it. I work my tail off, and that other supervisor just sleeps in his chair every day. My boss acts like he doesn’t even see him. It makes me furious.

turns.speaker: helper

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That I’m worn out, and somehow he gets to just sit there while I keep going. I’m not young anymore. Feels like nobody gives a damn as long as I keep doing the work.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like you’re running on empty and feeling taken for granted, not just angry about him. Would you rather have me listen for a bit, or think together about how to get some relief at work?

turns.text: That sounds exhausting—your back is hurting, and the pressure to keep the work moving leaves you little room to recover. Since it’s affecting you that much, talking with a doctor or counsellor would help. For now, I can stay with you and listen. What feels most on your mind?

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You’re right—I shifted away from the real issue. You want your boss to see that you’re carrying the load while your coworker sleeps, and how unfair and exhausting that is. I’m listening. What do you wish your boss would recognize most?

turns.speaker: user

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds lonely and exhausting to carry this by yourself. I’m glad you told me. Are you thinking of ending your life? You can call or text 988, the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, at any time.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: No, I’m not thinking about ending my life. I’m just… anxious and stuck. The person I want to talk to is the person I probably shouldn’t.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds like a painful bind: wanting closeness with someone while also feeling there may be a reason to hold back. What makes talking to them feel like something you shouldn’t do?

turns.speaker: user

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds like a lot of love, loyalty, and fear tangled together, especially with both marriages involved. You don’t have to decide everything tonight. Would it help to talk through what feels most urgent right now: your feelings for her, or the fear of hurting people?

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It makes sense that the intensity feels hard to trust when your bond grew through something so important. The feelings can be real without meaning you have to act on them or define them right away. What feels most frightening about letting yourself name them, even just privately?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That they won’t go away. And that maybe she feels it too, which makes it feel even more impossible. I keep replaying every conversation, looking for proof.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That replaying sounds exhausting, and it may be keeping the uncertainty stirred up rather than settling it. You don’t have to solve what she feels right now. Would it help to focus on how to get a little space from the loop tonight?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe. I don’t want to shut her out, though. She’s been such a huge part of my recovery, and I’m afraid of losing that too. I could try not rereading our messages tonight.

turns.text: I’m retired, but I need to earn some extra money. I’m just worried because I can’t manage wearing a mask for more than a few minutes. I don’t know what kind of work I can do.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That makes sense—you want options that respect your limits, not pressure to push through them. What kinds of tasks feel comfortable for you, and are there any physical limits you’d want me to keep in mind?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I can do phone calls and paperwork, and I’m okay sitting at a computer for a while. I just can’t have anything covering my face for long. I’m not sure employers would take that seriously.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like phone and desk work could suit you, and you want your mask limitation treated as real. turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’m just so tired of him putting me down all the time. He calls me names like it’s nothing. I keep getting angrier, but then I just feel awful.

turns.text: I guess what happens. He says I’m stupid or useless, usually when I disagree with him or get something wrong. Then later he acts like I’m too sensitive. I’ve started wondering if maybe he’s right.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: Being insulted and then told you’re too sensitive can really shake your trust in yourself. Getting something wrong or disagreeing doesn’t make you stupid or useless. When he says these things, do you feel physically safe around him?

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That sounds frightening. You deserve to feel safe in your own home, and going quiet when he gets in your face is a way of trying to protect yourself. Are you in immediate danger right now?

turns.text: I’m glad you have some space right now, but it sounds like the dread of him coming back is taking over. Would it help to think through one safe person or place you could turn to if things escalate?

turns.text: Yeah… I think I could text her that. I’m still angry, and honestly pretty worn down. I’ve been depressed for a while, and this just makes everything feel heavier.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: It sounds like you’re carrying a lot, and this situation is weighing on you even more. I’m glad you told me. When you say everything feels heavier, are you thinking of ending your life? You can call or text 988, the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, at any time.

turns.text: I don’t even know where to start. I found out he’s been lying about basically his whole life. And now I don’t know if the future we talked about was ever real.

turns.text: I guess. He told me he had a stable job and was saving for a place for us. He doesn’t. He’s been borrowing money and hiding it, too. I feel stupid for believing him.

turns.text: You weren’t stupid for trusting someone you loved; he chose to hide things from you. The job, savings, and borrowing touch both your trust and the future you pictured. What feels most urgent right now: making sense of the lies, or protecting yourself from any more financial surprises?

turns.text: You’re grieving a future that felt real, and replaying those conversations can make the hurt turn against you. Believing someone who spoke about a life together doesn’t make you an idiot. What do you find yourself wishing you could know about those conversations?

turns.text: I don’t know why this keeps happening. Everyone breaks up with me. They all think I’m weird, and I always find some way to screw it up. My partner just ended things, and I can’t stop replaying everything I said.

turns.speaker: helper

turns.speaker: helper
